## Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.11), tested at `55bfb4d7437bd4e09ab7cba58a43bd68eb310044` (`deepseek-harness` 0.2.0-rc.2) and re-checked against current `master` (0.2.1-alpha.3), which still has the same shape.

## Describe the bug

The source-built `deepseek-harness` ships **no usable Linux sandbox runner**. `dsh`'s sandbox seam is fail-closed: with no runner, every `bash` tool call (and every other confined tool execution) aborts before the command runs:

```
sandbox mode "workspace-write" is requested but no sandbox backend is usable on this host;
refusing to run the command unconfined. Install bubblewrap or run a Landlock-enforcing kernel
(Linux), ensure sandbox-exec is usable (macOS), or ensure the ACL restricted-token runner can
start (Windows) — otherwise switch the consumer to danger-full-access.
```

This is the default experience: `workspace-write` is the shipped permission preset, so the agent's shell is unusable out of the box and users are pushed toward `danger-full-access` (fully unconfined) to get anything done.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `nix build github:NixOS/nixpkgs/master#deepseek-harness`
2. Inspect the packaged native payload:
   ```
   $ ls -R result/libexec/dsh/native/system/packages/linux-x64/bin
   result/libexec/dsh/native/system/packages/linux-x64/bin:
   glibc

   result/libexec/dsh/native/system/packages/linux-x64/bin/glibc:
   system.node
   ```
   There is no `landlock-run`, and no `musl/system.node`.
3. `result/bin/dsh --profile web`, then in the web UI ask the agent to run any shell command under the default (`workspace-write`) permission preset.
4. The `bash` tool result is the `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` error quoted above; no process is ever spawned.

## Minimal reproducer

```nix
{
  inputs.nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/55bfb4d7437bd4e09ab7cba58a43bd68eb310044";

  outputs =
    { nixpkgs, ... }:
    let
      system = "x86_64-linux";
      pkgs = nixpkgs.legacyPackages.${system};
    in
    {
      packages.${system}.default = pkgs.deepseek-harness;
    };
}
```

`nix build` it and check `ls result/libexec/dsh/native/system/packages/linux-x64/bin/` — the launcher the sandbox probes for is absent; `result/bin/dsh` has no `bwrap` on its `PATH` either.

## Expected behaviour

`dsh` should have at least one Linux confinement backend available, as the npm-distributed artifacts do — either `bwrap` on the wrapper `PATH`, or the Landlock launcher binary — so that confined shell execution works. (If the sandbox is intentionally unsupported in the source build, the failure should at least be documented on the package, since it disables the product's default tool path.)

## Relevant log output

The error is produced by the sandbox seam (`SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE`, `packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/index.ts`) and surfaced by `dsh-bash-sandbox`:

```
sandbox mode "workspace-write" is requested but no sandbox backend is usable on this host;
refusing to run the command unconfined. …
```

Runner chain: Linux probes `bwrap` first, then the Landlock launcher (`packages/sandbox/sandbox-local/src/index.ts`, `PLATFORM_CHAINS`/`chainVerdict`). Both probes fail here:

```
$ command -v bwrap
(none)

$ ls result/libexec/dsh/native/system/packages/linux-x64/bin
glibc

$ ls result/libexec/dsh/native/system/packages/linux-x64/bin/glibc
system.node
```

Upstream's own packager docs warn about exactly this (`native/system/scripts/verify-launcher-binary.mjs`): without its prepack gate, a checkout that never ran `pnpm run build:native` ships an EMPTY platform package — "the binary's absence surfacing only at runtime as a failed probe on every consumer".

## Additional context

### Root cause

The repo's root `package.json` defines `build:native-system` as `tsx native/system/scripts/build.ts --host-addon-only`, and the top-level build script (`scripts/build.ts`) invokes it. That flag exists for packagers and **skips non-Node-API payloads**, i.e. exactly `bin/landlock-run` (declared `kind: static-musl` in `native/system/packages/linux-x64/prebuilds.json`).

The npm artifacts don't have this problem because the published platform package ships the launcher:

```
$ curl -sL https://registry.npmjs.org/@deepseek-ai/node-addon-system-linux-x64/-/node-addon-system-linux-x64-0.1.2.tgz | tar tzf -
package/bin/landlock-run
package/LICENSE
package/package.json
package/prebuilds.json
package/bin/glibc/system.node
package/bin/musl/system.node
```

That is why the npm-tarball inits don't hit this: #552467's test plan says it "probes Landlock enforcement" (the tarball carries the binary), and #553134 additionally puts `bubblewrap` on the wrapper `PATH` for Linux. Both are still open; the merged recipe (#571214, then #573598 and #574341) is source-built and drops the launcher.

The `passthru.tests.web-boot` test only boots the web profile and greps for `<!doctype html>`, so nixpkgs CI stays green while the product's default tool path is broken.

### Suggested fixes (both verified on this host)

Both fixes were validated on `x86_64-linux`, Linux 7.2.10, LSM list `capability,landlock,yama,bpf,ima`:

1. **Put `bubblewrap` on the wrapper `PATH`** (the upstream error text names it first) — same approach as #553134:
   ```nix
   makeBinaryWrapper ${nodejs_24}/bin/node $out/bin/dsh \
     --prefix PATH : ${lib.makeBinPath [ pnpm_11 bubblewrap ]} \
     --add-flags "--expose-internals $out/libexec/dsh/apps/cli/lib/bin.js"
   ```
   The first rung's probe is `bwrap --ro-bind / / --dev /dev --unshare-pid --proc /proc --die-with-parent -- true`, which exits 0 here.

2. **Ship the Landlock launcher**, either by running `native/system/scripts/build.ts` without `--host-addon-only` (needs `musl-gcc`), or by installing `bin/landlock-run` from the matching `@deepseek-ai/node-addon-system-<platform>-<arch>` npm tarball. The npm binary runs here and probes cleanly:
   ```
   $ ./package/bin/landlock-run --probe
   landlock: fully enforced
   ```

Either one fixes the default sandbox path without changing the rest of the recipe.

- VS Code Version: 1.138.0 (7debcd0e2acdea1c52de81bf9ee1620444407dda), Universal build
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), Apple silicon

The Universal (darwin-universal) build's `Info.plist` has no `NSAppleEventsUsageDescription`. The darwin-arm64 and darwin (Intel) builds of the same version have it ("An application in Visual Studio Code wants to use AppleScript.").

macOS attributes Apple Events sent by programs run in the integrated terminal to VS Code. Without the usage description, it refuses them without asking the user and records nothing, so System Settings › Privacy & Security › Automation never lists the target app under Visual Studio Code, and there is no switch to turn on. Command-line tools that send Apple Events fail with `errAEEventNotPermitted` (-1743). `osascript` is the exception: it can still make macOS ask.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Install the Universal build of VS Code 1.138.0.
2. Open Notes. Visual Studio Code must not have been allowed or denied control of Notes yet.
3. In the integrated terminal, save this as `repro.swift`, then run `swiftc repro.swift -o repro && ./repro`:

```swift
import AppKit

// Asks macOS for permission to send Apple Events to Notes, letting it prompt.
guard let notes = NSRunningApplication.runningApplications(withBundleIdentifier: "com.apple.Notes").first else {
    print("open Notes first")
    exit(1)
}
let target = NSAppleEventDescriptor(processIdentifier: notes.processIdentifier)
print(AEDeterminePermissionToAutomateTarget(target.aeDesc, typeWildCard, typeWildCard, true))
```

Expected: macOS asks whether "Visual Studio Code" may control "Notes".

Actual: `-1743` is printed at once, with no prompt. tccd logs:

```
Refusing TCCAccessRequestIndirect for service kTCCServiceAppleEvents and client /Applications/Visual Studio Code.app[0] without NSAppleEventsUsageDescription key
```

The key is in the Universal build up to 1.103 and missing from 1.104 on. It looks like the step in `build/darwin/sign.ts` that adds it now runs after the per-architecture archives are made, and the Universal build is assembled from those archives (#261850). The key was added in 325bea69a747db9cd487c708684108f85dd4eff3 (#119787).

Workaround: run `osascript -e 'tell application "Notes" to get name'` once in the integrated terminal to get the prompt, or install the darwin-arm64 or darwin build.

Related: #307364 (child processes can't reach other TCC-protected resources).

When you send a steering message while the Copilot agent is working, tool results from around that moment can show as cancelled and lose their output, even though the work ran. This makes it look as if steering killed the agent's background agents. The agents keep running; only the chat loses track of their results.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open the Chat view (or the Agents window) and pick the Copilot agent (Agent Host).
2. Ask it to make several small file edits one at a time, or to start a background agent that edits files or runs commands.
3. While it is working, type a steering message and press Enter.

## Expected
- The edit or command that finished just before your message shows as completed, with its diff or output.
- A background agent's edits and commands keep completing in that agent's chat.
- Your steering message starts a new request below.

## Actual
- The edit or command that finished just before your message shows as cancelled (skipped), and its diff or output is missing.
- A background agent's edit or command that finishes at that moment never completes in that agent's chat, and is later shown as cancelled. The same happens when you send a new message while a background agent is editing.

## Cause
The runtime only shows the steering message after the current round of tools has finished, and it moves a foreground agent to the background instead of stopping it. VS Code records some results (file edits, shell output) asynchronously after the runtime reports a tool as done. When the steering message arrives, VS Code ends the running turn immediately. Ending a turn marks its unfinished tool calls as cancelled, and later updates to that turn are ignored. VS Code also dropped a background agent's pending result whenever the main chat's turn changed, even though the result belongs to the agent's own chat. VS Code does not call abort or cancel for any agent or task when you steer.

## Notes
- Seen in the editor Chat view with the Copilot agent: sending a steering message right after starting a turn made running background agents look like they were killed. The same code path is used by the Agents window.
- Confirmed with deterministic Agent Host tests on `main` at `dc811b77cd1`, not with a live model run (test sign-in was unavailable). The runtime was checked by reading its source: steering with `mode: 'immediate'` moves a foreground agent to the background and does not cancel background agents.

# Agents: PDF webview returns 401 for an allowed vscode-agent-host resource with matching _ah metadata

## Summary

A PDF opened from a remote agent-host filesystem in the Agents window fails with "Unexpected server response" and zero pages. The PDF extension correctly includes the document's parent directory in `localResourceRoots`.

VS Code's webview loader strips the query from the requested URI but not from the allowed root. Both originally carry the same `_ah` agent-host routing metadata. The shared URI containment helper compares queries, so the modified request no longer matches its allowed parent. VS Code returns 401 before attempting the file read.

This was diagnosed and temporarily worked around in the running application using dbgjs. Changing only this viewer's allowed-root query to empty changed the request from 401 to 200, after which the same PDF rendered successfully.

## Environment

| Item | Observed value |
| --- | --- |
| Investigation date | 2026-10-18 |
| VS Code | 1.143.0-insider |
| Installed commit | `9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0` |
| Build date | 2026-10-15 |
| Client OS | Windows build 26100, ARM64 |
| Window | Agents |
| Resource provider | Remote `vscode-agent-host` connection over WSS |
| Extension | `tomoki1207.pdf` 1.2.2 |
| PDF.js | 2.10.377, build `156762c48` |
| Test document | A valid 13,264-byte PDF 1.4 document containing one page |
| Current upstream checked | `dc811b77cd1e0753d306b0c6f819a7311bcf49b5` |

The installed and checked upstream versions of `resourceLoading.ts` are textually identical. This is source confirmation, not an end-to-end run of the newer build.

The exact remote OS and first affected release were not established. No remote credentials, real connection authority, or document contents are required for this report.

## UI reproduction

Preconditions: an existing remote agent-host connection in Agents and the PDF extension installed.

1. Put a valid PDF in a directory on the remote filesystem.
2. Open that remote PDF with the PDF custom editor.
3. Ensure its resource is represented as a `vscode-agent-host` URI with `_ah` metadata, and that the extension derives its allowed parent directory by changing only the URI path.
4. Observe zero pages and the red "Unexpected server response" banner.
5. Expand "More Information": PDF.js reports an unexpected server response with status 401.

These steps describe the observed setup. A clean-machine provisioning recipe and independent end-to-end reproduction on another machine have not been executed.

### Expected

A PDF below an explicitly allowed directory, with matching host and backing-resource identity, is loaded and rendered.

### Actual

The webview denies access before file reading, returning:

```text
HTTP status: 401
Body: Unauthorized
PDF.js: Unexpected server response (401) while retrieving PDF
```

The extension's scripts and styles load; only the document request fails.

## Sanitized URI pair

The following preserves the relevant structure of the runtime values:

```text
Request:
vscode-agent-host://test-host/allowed/file.pdf?_ah=eyJzY2hlbWUiOiJmaWxlIn0

Allowed root:
vscode-agent-host://test-host/allowed/?_ah=eyJzY2hlbWUiOiJmaWxlIn0
```

The query above is the URI object's `query` value, not a claim about serialized URL escaping. `URI.toString()` can display the equals sign percent-encoded.

Here `_ah` decodes to `{"scheme":"file"}`. It is routing metadata, not an authentication token.

## Root cause and source references

All links in this section are pinned to the installed commit.

1. The extension retains the document query when deriving its parent directory. The installed extension's `out/src/pdfPreview.js:16` uses `resource.with({ path: ... })`, and line 21 sets `localResourceRoots: [resourceRoot, extensionRoot]`.
2. [Agent-host URI wrapping](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostUri.ts#L107) stores the original resource identity in `_ah`.
3. [getResourceToLoad, line 120](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/browser/resourceLoading.ts#L120) clears the request query.
4. [The containment call, line 128](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/browser/resourceLoading.ts#L128) still passes the unchanged root.
5. [ExtUri.isEqualOrParent, line 173](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/base/common/resources.ts#L173) checks the scheme, authority, path, and query. [Line 191](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/base/common/resources.ts#L191) explicitly requires query equality. `ignoreFragment: true` does not ignore queries.
6. [WebviewElement, line 966](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/browser/webviewElement.ts#L966) converts `AccessDenied` into status 401.

This 401 is generated by VS Code's webview authorization layer. It is not evidence of a remote server authentication failure.

## Runtime evidence

A non-pausing dbgjs logpoint inside `getResourceToLoad` inspected the actual request, roots, and `IUriIdentityService`. Using the live comparator produced:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Request with query cleared against original root | `false` |
| Original request against original root | `true` |
| Query cleared from both request and root | `true` |
| Request against the extension's unrelated installation root | `false` |

A viewer-frame fetch independently reproduced 401 with the literal body `Unauthorized`.

### Controlled live workaround

With the user's approval, a one-shot dbgjs logpoint replaced only the matching root in this viewer's `localResourceRoots` array with `root.with({ query: '' })`. It did not add a directory, alter the root path/authority, clear the request metadata, or patch the global authorization function.

The patch trigger was removed before reopening the document in PDF.js.

Verified outcome:

```json
{
  "fetch": {
    "status": 200,
    "bytes": 13264,
    "header": "%PDF-1.4"
  },
  "viewer": {
    "pages": 1,
    "page": 1,
    "renderingState": 3,
    "canvasWidth": 1392,
    "canvasHeight": 1971,
    "errorVisible": false
  }
}
```

The fetch and viewer observations were collected in separate calls and combined here. This is a temporary workaround, not validation of a production patch. It lasts only for this viewer instance. All investigation logpoints were removed and debugger connections disconnected.

## Proposed regression test

Add a focused test to the existing [resourceLoading.test.ts suite](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/test/browser/resourceLoading.test.ts#L21), using its existing `uriIdentityService` setup:

```ts
test('Allows an agent-host file below a root with matching routing metadata', () => {
    const resource = URI.from({
        scheme: 'vscode-agent-host',
        authority: 'test-host',
        path: '/allowed/file.pdf',
        query: '_ah=eyJzY2hlbWUiOiJmaWxlIn0',
    });
    const root = resource.with({ path: '/allowed/' });

    const result = getResourceToLoad(resource, [root], uriIdentityService);

    assert.strictEqual(result?.toString(), resource.toString());
});
```

This is a proposed test, not an executed repository test. It directly models the observed runtime inputs and expected preservation of routing metadata.

## Permanent fix requirements

Ownership belongs primarily in VS Code's webview/agent-host resource authorization integration, rather than PDF parsing.

The initial idea of stripping both queries indiscriminately is not a sufficiently justified production fix:

- [Agent-host metadata](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostUri.ts#L59) can carry the original scheme, authority, query, a different backing content path, content-reference routing, and file identity. For those URIs, the displayed path alone does not necessarily identify what will be read.
- [Existing containment tests, line 342](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/test/browser/resourceLoading.test.ts#L342) explicitly expect a query-bearing `vscode-remote` root to remain rejected. A generic query-stripping change would alter that behavior.
- [Existing query tests, line 363](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/test/browser/resourceLoading.test.ts#L363) verify request-query preservation with queryless roots, but do not cover this positive agent-host request/root pair.

Recommended direction:

1. Add the failing regression test first.
2. Define a narrow, scheme-aware containment rule for plain agent-host filesystem URIs carrying compatible backing-resource metadata. Preserve/validate that identity rather than globally discarding `_ah`.
3. For content references or metadata that changes the effective backing path, check the actual resolved identity or retain explicit conservative rejection until a policy is defined.
4. Preserve the original request URI when calling the file service, including query and fragment.
5. Keep other schemes' existing behavior unless an intentional, separately reviewed change is needed. Do not globally change `ExtUri.isEqualOrParent`.

Additional required tests:

- Matching plain-file `_ah` request/root succeeds and returns the original URI.
- Different hosts, different backing identities, siblings, outside-root paths, and root-equals-resource remain rejected.

### Describe the bug

On a non-NixOS Linux host whose ALSA default device is PipeWire, `claude-code` voice mode cannot open the microphone:

```
ALSA lib dlmisc.c:339:(snd_dlobj_cache_get0) [error.core] Cannot open shared library libasound_module_pcm_pipewire.so (/nix/store/xlqm12gx3s3f7dc1a5pnfk4p2niw2lri-alsa-lib-1.2.16.1/lib/alsa-lib/libasound_module_pcm_pipewire.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory)
```

On Linux, the wrapper adds `--prefix LD_LIBRARY_PATH : ${lib.makeLibraryPath [ alsa-lib ]}`. That alsa-lib reads the host's ALSA configuration (here `/etc/alsa/conf.d/99-pipewire-default.conf` from Ubuntu's `pipewire-alsa`, which routes `default` to the `pipewire` PCM type). It then looks for the plugin in its own `lib/alsa-lib`, which does not exist. alsa-lib honors `ALSA_PLUGIN_DIR` (`src/dlmisc.c`).

`alsa-utils` already solves this: its wrapper sets `--set-default ALSA_PLUGIN_DIR` to a `symlinkJoin` of `alsa-plugins` and `pipewire` (`withPipewireLib ? true`).

### Steps to reproduce

This uses the same alsa-lib store path as `claude-code`, through the unwrapped `alsa-utils` binary, on a host where ALSA's default device is PipeWire:

1. `au=$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths github:NixOS/nixpkgs/8edc0c72e3a38faf5434e40d1f19431125fe4b30#alsa-utils)`
2. `env -u ALSA_PLUGIN_DIR "$au/bin/.aplay-wrapped" --capture --duration=1 --format=S16_LE --rate=16000 /dev/null`: prints the error above, then `audio open error: No such device or address`, exit 1.
3. `pw=$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths github:NixOS/nixpkgs/8edc0c72e3a38faf5434e40d1f19431125fe4b30#pipewire)`
4. `ALSA_PLUGIN_DIR="$pw/lib/alsa-lib" "$au/bin/.aplay-wrapped" --capture --duration=1 --format=S16_LE --rate=16000 /dev/null`: records, exit 0.

In `claude-code` itself, enabling voice mode and starting dictation prints the same error.

### Expected behaviour

Voice mode records from the host's default ALSA device, as `alsa-utils` from the same nixpkgs does.

### Additional context

Workaround, applied locally with Home Manager; with it, `/voice` no longer prints the ALSA error:

```nix
pkgs.symlinkJoin {
  name = "claude-code-${pkgs.claude-code.version}";
  paths = [ pkgs.claude-code ];
  nativeBuildInputs = [ pkgs.makeWrapper ];
  postBuild = ''
    wrapProgram "$out/bin/claude" \
      --set-default ALSA_PLUGIN_DIR "${pkgs.pipewire}/lib/alsa-lib"
  '';
}
```

A packaging fix could follow `alsa-utils` and add `--set-default ALSA_PLUGIN_DIR` next to the existing `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` prefix. Two tradeoffs for the maintainers:

- Closure size: `pipewire`'s runtime closure added about 565 MiB to my profile. A `withPipewireLib`-style flag, as in `alsa-utils`, would keep that opt-out.
- Inheritance: like the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` prefix, the variable reaches every command `claude` runs. Host-built ALSA programs started from Claude would then load the Nix plugin.

## Describe the bug

In a Copilot CLI (Agent Host) session, every `*.instructions.md` file in `~/.copilot/instructions` appears twice in the system prompt. A Local chat session shows it once. The setting `chat.instructionsFilesLocations` does not change this.

The duplicate doubles the context cost of all user-level instruction files.

## Environment (clean install)

- Windows 11 Enterprise 25H2 (build 26200), clean VM, default settings
- VS Code 1.142.0 (stable, user installer), built-in GitHub Copilot Chat 0.70.0, no other extensions
- Bundled `@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.19-unstable.38345923974.g3754b70

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create `%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\instructions\zz-dup-test.instructions.md`:

   ```markdown
   ---
   description: dup test marker. USE WHEN: never.
   applyTo: "**"
   ---

   # ZZ-DUP-TEST-MARKER

   This is a temporary marker file for duplicate-registration testing.
   ```

2. Open Chat, switch the session target from **Local** to **Copilot CLI**, start a new session and ask: "How many times does an instruction body with the heading ZZ-DUP-TEST-MARKER appear in your context?"

Result: **Local = 1**, **Copilot CLI = 2**. In the Copilot CLI session, `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl` has a `system.message` event in which the marker body appears twice, back to back.

## Root cause (from reading the 1.142.0 source)

1. `SessionDiscoveredEntry` asks the SDK to discover customizations (`rpc.instructions.discover`). Rules found in `~/.copilot/instructions` come back as `RuleCustomization`.
2. `mapToParsedPlugin()` in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts` turns those discovered rules into a synthetic "session plugin" with `instructions`.
3. `_appliedPlugins()` adds that session plugin to `plugins`.
4. `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSessionLauncher.ts` builds `instructionDirectories = toSdkInstructionDirectories(plugins.flatMap(p => p.instructions))` and passes it to `createSession` together with `enableConfigDiscovery: true`.
5. The runtime loads `~/.copilot/instructions` through its own discovery and again through the explicit `instructionDirectories`, and does not deduplicate them when it assembles the system prompt.

A comment in the launcher already says it relies on the SDK for discovery "to avoid duplicates", but instructions discovered by the SDK are still fed back.

## Verification

SDK only (`@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.22, no VS Code). I counted a heading in the `system.message` event, with `enableConfigDiscovery: true` and the real `~/.copilot/instructions`:

| `instructionDirectories` | occurrences |
|---|---|
| not set | 1 |
| `["C:\\Users\\<u>\\.copilot\\instructions"]` | 2 |
| `["c:\\Users\\<u>\\.copilot\\instructions"]` | 2 |
| same directory, with `enableConfigDiscovery: false` | 2 |

So this is not a drive-letter-case problem: explicit `instructionDirectories` that equal the home instructions directory are not deduplicated. `session.rpc.instructions.getSources()` still reports one entry, so that API hides the problem.

In the clean VM, I patched the compiled `agentHostMain.js` so that `instructionDirectories:M` became `instructionDirectories:[]`, restarted VS Code and asked the same question in a Copilot CLI session. The marker then appeared **once** (system message: 33,767 chars with 2 copies before, 32,499 chars with 1 copy after).

The plain `copilot` CLI 1.0.100-1 does not pass `instructionDirectories` and injects the files once.

## Suggested fix

- VS Code (minimal): do not forward instructions that the SDK discovered itself. For example, build the session plugin from discovered agents and skills only (`instructions: []`), or exclude discovered rules whose directory SDK discovery already covers when computing `instructionDirectories`.
- Runtime: canonicalize (realpath, case-insensitive on Windows) and deduplicate explicit `instructionDirectories` against home and discovered instruction sources before building the prompt.

## Caveats

- I did not check whether disabling an individual discovered instruction in the customizations UI relies on this path. `instructionDirectories` works per directory.
- Other discovered locations (for example `.github/instructions` in a workspace) use the same code path and may be affected too. I have not tested them.

1.143 changes how the Agents window stores sessions and nested sessions, while keeping older builds compatible. This test checks that your sessions survive an upgrade from 1.142 to 1.143, a downgrade back, and an upgrade again.

## Setup

1. Unpack the latest 1.142.x stable and the 1.143 build linked [here](https://builds.code.visualstudio.com/builds/stable?commit=bd48654d9acb491371090b13841cff4dd1888fc8) into two separate folders, for example `~/tpi/1.142` and `~/tpi/1.143` (macOS/Windows `.zip`, Linux `.tar.gz`). Don't create a `data` folder next to them.
2. Launch **1.142** with a fresh test profile folder, `~/tpi-agents-data` (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\tpi-agents-data`), opening the Agents window directly. Both builds use this same folder:

   | OS | 1.142 | 1.143 |
   |---|---|---|
   | macOS | `~/tpi/1.142/Visual\ Studio\ Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/bin/code --user-data-dir ~/tpi-agents-data --agents` | the same, with `1.143` |
   | Windows (cmd) | `%USERPROFILE%\tpi\1.142\bin\code.cmd --user-data-dir %USERPROFILE%\tpi-agents-data --agents` | the same, with `1.143` |
   | Linux | `~/tpi/1.142/VSCode-linux-x64/bin/code --user-data-dir ~/tpi-agents-data --agents` | the same, with `1.143` |

3. Sign in to GitHub. Then open **Settings** (<kbd>Cmd+,</kbd> / <kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>, or **Settings** in the account menu):
   - search `update.mode` and set **Update: Mode** to `none`, so 1.142 doesn't update itself during the test;
   - search `chat.agentHost.codexAgent.enabled` and check **Codex Agent: Enabled** (marked Experimental; it's off by default in stable). If it's greyed out, your organization manages it: skip Codex.
4. Quit 1.142 and launch it again with the same command.

Your normal VS Code can stay open, because it uses a different data folder.

> **Never run 1.142 and 1.143 at the same time.** Quit one completely (all windows) before you launch the other.

## How to test

Run both scenarios with **Copilot** sessions. Then do a quick sanity pass with **Claude** and **Codex** sessions: pick a few steps from each scenario; there's no need to do every step for every harness.

## Scenario 1: Upgrade from 1.142 to 1.143

1. In **1.142**, create Copilot sessions in the disposable repository:
   - sessions in the repository folder and sessions in a **worktree**;
   - sessions with one or two **nested sessions** (**New Nested Session**), and a session whose chat history has a **subagent** pill (for example "use a subagent to list the files in this folder");
   - **Rename...** sessions that have no nested sessions, and some nested sessions (not the main session). Don't rename a session that has nested sessions (see Known limitations);
   - **Mark as Done** a session, and a nested session from its context menu;
   - leave some sessions and nested sessions unread, and **Mark as Read** others;
   - a session with **changes** (let the agent edit files), and one with a **pull request** and **artifacts** (for example "open a draft PR with this change");
   - change the mode or approvals of a session;
   - **Mark as Done** one **worktree** session, and **Delete...** another.
2. Enable **Done** in the **Filter** menu, then take screenshots of the session list (expand the projects) and of 2–3 sessions with nested sessions. Quit 1.142.
3. Launch **1.143** with the same profile.
   - **Expected:** the session list appears without a long hang, and the CPU settles within a minute or two.
4. Compare with your screenshots.
   - **Expected:** every session and nested session is listed once, under the same project, in the same order, with the same title, worktree icon, unread state, done state, changes (except done worktree sessions, see Known limitations), pull request and artifacts.
   - **Expected:** the deleted worktree session is still gone.
5. Open each session with nested sessions.
   - **Expected:** the main session and the same nested sessions appear in the same order, with the same titles and the same done and unread states, and each shows its full chat history. The subagent pill opens the subagent. Each nested session has the session's mode and approvals.
6. Send a message in the main session of an old session and in one of its nested sessions.
   - **Expected:** the replies stream normally below the old chat history.
7. Quit and launch 1.143 again.
   - **Expected:** everything from steps 4–6 is still the same.

## Scenario 2: Downgrade to 1.142 and upgrade again

### (a) Changes in 1.143, checked in 1.142

1. In **1.143**, make changes you can recognize (with distinctive names):
   - **Rename...** a session that has nested sessions, and one of its nested sessions;
   - **Mark as Done** a nested session and a session, and **Restore** another done session;
   - **Mark as Unread** a nested session, and **Mark as Read** another one;
   - create a nested session in an old session, and a new session with a nested session;
   - **Mark as Done** a worktree session that has uncommitted changes, and **Delete...** another worktree session.
   - **Expected (worktrees):** a few seconds after marking it as done, the worktree folder is gone, and its branch exists with a commit of the uncommitted changes. After deleting, the folder is gone and the branch still exists.
2. Quit 1.143 and launch **1.142**.
   - **Expected:** 1.142 lists and opens everything, including the nested sessions and sessions created in 1.143. Every change from step 1 shows as you left it.
3. Send a message in a nested session created in 1.143.
   - **Expected:** it works.

### (b) Changes in 1.142, checked in 1.143

1. Still in **1.142**, make changes you can recognize:
   - **Rename...** a session from scenario 1 that has nested sessions, and one of its nested sessions;
   - **Mark as Done** a nested session and a session;
   - create a nested session in an existing session, and type a draft in it without sending;
   - create a new session;
   - **Delete...** a nested session, and **Delete...** a session.
2. Quit 1.142 and launch **1.143**.
   - **Expected:** every 1.142 change shows. The new nested session has its draft, and the new session is there.
   - **Expected:** nothing is lost, listed twice or reverted to how it was in (a). The deleted nested session and session don't come back, not even empty.
3. **Restore** the worktree session you marked as done in (a), and send a message.
   - **Expected:** it works in its worktree again.
4. Quit and launch 1.143 again.
   - **Expected:** the result of steps 2–3 is unchanged.

## Known limitations

- Known issue (no need to test or report): a session with nested sessions that was renamed in 1.142 **before** the first upgrade shows its previous title in 1.143.
- A worktree session marked as done, whose worktree folder was removed, may show no changes in 1.143, and its Branch Changes says "Branch changes are unavailable because the session's folder is not a Git repository or no longer exists." 1.143 computes changes from Git instead of keeping a stored copy.

## What to report

For each problem, include the scenario and step, which build made the change and which build shows the problem, the provider, and before/after screenshots. Attach the logs from **Developer: Export Agent Host Debug Logs...** in the build that shows the problem. If that fails, attach `agenthost.log` from **Developer: Open Logs Folder** (the newest folder).

When you're done, delete `~/tpi-agents-data` and the disposable repository.

New Copilot chats in the Agents window and the agent-host Chat view can now start their runtime and MCP servers **before you send the first message**. Your customizations are ready sooner, and the first reply should start faster. If you never send, nothing is saved and the session doesn't appear in your list.

This is off by default, behind an experimental setting.

## Setup

- Add this to your user settings:
  ```json
  "chat.agentHost.experimental.prewarmSessions": true
  ```
- Have at least one local MCP server configured, for example in your workspace's `.mcp.json`:
  ```json
  { "mcpServers": { "everything": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything"] } } }
  ```
- Use a trusted folder that is a git repository.
- To see what's happening, open the **Agent Host** output channel or log file (Command Palette: **Developer: Open Logs Folder** → `agenthost.log`) and look for lines containing `[warm]`.

## Scenario 1: A new chat warms up before you send

1. In the Agents window, start a new Copilot session for your folder. Don't send anything yet.
2. In the log, check that you see `[warm] Started pre-warmed session`.
3. Check that your MCP server is already running before you've sent anything (for example in your OS process list, or in the session's MCP servers list).
4. Send a short message. Check that:
   - you see `[warm] Claimed pre-warmed session` in the log, and only one session was started for the chat;
   - the chat works normally, and the session now appears in your session list.

## Scenario 2: Send right away

1. Start a new session and send a message immediately, without waiting.
2. Check that the chat works normally and only one session was started.

## Scenario 3: Abandon a chat

1. Start a new session and wait for it to warm up, but don't send.
2. Switch the draft to a different workspace or close it.
3. Check that you see `[warm] Discarded pre-warmed session` in the log, and the MCP server it started stops.
4. Check that the abandoned chat never shows up in your session list, including after restarting VS Code.

## Scenario 4: Change things before sending

1. In a new, warmed-up session, change the model and the mode, then send. The session should be **claimed** (reused).
2. In another new session, wait for it to warm up, then add or remove a server in `.mcp.json`. The log should show a **discard** followed by a new **start**. Then send, and check that it's claimed.

## Scenario 5: Worktree and Quick Chat

1. Start a new session with isolation set to **New Worktree** and send. The worktree is created and the chat works normally. The warmed folder session is discarded at Send. This is expected: a worktree chat always starts its own session cold.
2. Start a **Quick Chat** (no folder). Check that it warms up and is claimed when you send.

## Scenario 6: Setting off

1. Remove the setting, or set it to `false`.
2. Start a new session and check that there are no `[warm]` lines and no MCP server starts until you send. Everything should work exactly as before.

The Migrations view can now move MCP servers that use `oauth` to the Copilot format, instead of leaving them behind. The client ID is kept as `oauthClientId`. Servers that need something Copilot can't read stay in `mcp.json`: a client secret stored in VS Code, or enterprise-managed sign-in.

## Setup

1. Use a temporary profile.
2. Add this to User Settings (JSON):

   ```json
   "chat.customizations.migration.enabled": true
   ```

3. Open a folder and create `.vscode/mcp.json` with these servers. The URLs don't need to be reachable.

   ```jsonc
   {
     "servers": {
       "oauth-public": { "type": "http", "url": "https://example.com/public/mcp", "oauth": { "clientId": "public-client" } },
       "oauth-not-managed": { "type": "http", "url": "https://example.com/not-managed/mcp", "oauth": { "clientId": "public-client", "enterpriseManaged": false } },
       "oauth-secret": { "type": "http", "url": "https://example.com/secret/mcp", "oauth": { "clientId": "confidential-client" } },
       "oauth-managed": { "type": "http", "url": "https://example.com/managed/mcp", "oauth": { "clientId": "managed-client", "enterpriseManaged": true } }
     }
   }
   ```

4. In `.vscode/mcp.json`, select **Set Client Secret** above `oauth-secret`'s `clientId` and enter any test value.
5. Start a Copilot agent session in that folder so Copilot is the active harness.

## Test

1. Run **Chat: Open Customizations** and open **Migrations → Migrate MCP Servers**.
2. Verify `oauth-public` and `oauth-not-managed` are offered, each with the warning "You may need to sign in again after migration."
3. Verify these are not offered, and that their details explain why:
   - `oauth-secret`: its client secret is stored in VS Code, which Copilot can't use.
   - `oauth-managed`: enterprise-managed sign-in relies on a VS Code setting that Copilot doesn't have.
4. Migrate the two offered servers. Verify that:
   - they're removed from `.vscode/mcp.json`;
   - the folder's root `.mcp.json` has them with `"oauthClientId"` and no `oauth` or `enterpriseManaged`.
5. Select **Replace Client Secret** above `oauth-secret`'s `clientId` and delete the secret with the trash button. Reopen the migration page and verify `oauth-secret` is now offered.
6. Leave the migration page open and set the secret again. Then migrate `oauth-secret`, and verify it fails and stays in `.vscode/mcp.json`.
7. Copy `oauth-public` into your user `mcp.json` (**MCP: Open User Configuration**) and migrate it. Verify that:
   - it moves to `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` with `"oauthClientId"`;
   - the migration page also warns "VS Code will ask you to trust this server again after migration."

### Optional: sign in

If you have a real MCP server that requires OAuth with a pre-registered client ID (no client secret), add it with `"oauth": { "clientId": "..." }`, sign in, then migrate it. Verify that:

- it still connects from `.mcp.json` in VS Code's chat, using the same client;
- in a Copilot agent session, **Sign in** on the server opens the browser and the server connects.

## Cleanup

Delete the test servers from `.mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json`, your user `mcp.json` and `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`. Then delete the temporary profile.

---

When you migrate MCP servers to Copilot with **Chat: Open Customizations** → **Migrations**, servers that use a setting through `${config:...}` used to be skipped. They now migrate, and each setting becomes an environment variable set to the setting's current value. For example, `${config:mcp.test.port}` becomes `MCP_TEST_PORT`.

A few rules to know while testing:

- Only string and number values are copied. Anything else (unset, an object, a boolean) becomes an **empty** variable that you can fill in later.
- For a **workspace** server, only values from the workspace settings (`.vscode/settings.json`) are copied, because the new `.mcp.json` is usually committed. Values from your user settings become empty.
- For a **user** server, values from your user settings are copied, since it moves to your own Copilot config.
- The value is copied once. Changing the setting later doesn't update the migrated server.

## Setup

1. Use the latest Insiders build, ideally with a temporary profile.
2. Add this to your user settings:
   ```json
   "chat.customizations.migration.enabled": true,
   "mcp.test.userOnly": "from-user-settings"
   ```
3. Open a folder (a scratch git repo is fine) and start a **Copilot** agent session, so Copilot is the active harness.

The servers below don't need to actually run. You're checking what the migration writes.

## Scenario 1: Workspace server

1. Create `.vscode/settings.json` in the folder:
   ```json
   { "mcp.test.port": 8080 }
   ```
2. Create `.vscode/mcp.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "servers": {
       "config-stdio": {
         "command": "node",
         "args": ["server.js", "--port=${config:mcp.test.port}", "--user=${config:mcp.test.userOnly}"],
         "env": { "PORT": "${config:mcp.test.port}" }
       },
       "config-http": {
         "type": "http",
         "url": "https://example.com/mcp",
         "headers": { "X-Port": "${config:mcp.test.port}" }
       },
       "config-unset": {
         "command": "node",
         "args": ["--value=${config:mcp.test.doesNotExist}"]
       }
     }
   }
   ```
3. Run **Chat: Open Customizations** and open **Migrations**.
4. Check that all three servers are offered. Each one shows the warning **"Configs will become environment variables. Later changes won't apply."**
5. Migrate them, then open `.mcp.json` at the root of the folder and check:
   - `config-stdio`: `args` contains `--port=${MCP_TEST_PORT}` and `--user=${MCP_TEST_USER_ONLY}`. Its `env` has `PORT: "8080"`, `MCP_TEST_PORT: "8080"` and `MCP_TEST_USER_ONLY: ""`. The user-settings value is **not** copied.
   - `config-http`: the header is `${MCP_TEST_PORT:-8080}`.
   - `config-unset`: `args` contains `--value=${MCP_TEST_DOES_NOT_EXIST}`, and the variable is empty in `env`.
6. Check that the servers were removed from `.vscode/mcp.json`.
7. Open a migrated server's details in Customizations. Check that the empty variable shows **Key** / **Value** as placeholders.

## Scenario 2: User server

1. Run **MCP: Open User Configuration** and add:
   ```json
   "config-user": {
     "command": "node",
     "args": ["--user=${config:mcp.test.userOnly}"]
   }
   ```
2. Open **Migrations** and migrate `config-user`.
3. Open `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` and check that `args` contains `--user=${MCP_TEST_USER_ONLY}`, and `env` has `MCP_TEST_USER_ONLY: "from-user-settings"`. This time, the user-settings value **is** copied.

## Scenario 3: The setting changes before you migrate

1. Add another server with `${config:mcp.test.port}` to `.vscode/mcp.json`, and open **Migrations** so it's listed.
2. Without closing the view, change `mcp.test.port` in `.vscode/settings.json` to `9090`.
3. Migrate it. Check that it fails with a message saying the source configuration changed, and nothing is written.
4. Reopen **Migrations** and migrate again. It now succeeds with `9090`.

## Known limitations (no need to file)

- In VS Code's own chat, a migrated `${NAME}` in a stdio server's `command` or `args` stays literal, because VS Code expands it only from its process environment, not from the server's `env`. Copilot fills it from `env`.
- A remote server's setting value containing `}` is written as is, so it may not read back exactly.

## Cleanup

Delete `.mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json` and `.vscode/settings.json` from the folder, remove the test server from `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`, and delete the temporary profile.

Copilot can't prompt for VS Code's `${input:}` values or read VS Code settings through `${config:}`. MCP servers that used them used to be left behind when you migrated your MCP servers to Copilot. Now **Migrate** moves them too, and turns each input and setting into an environment variable. Servers that use OAuth now migrate as well.

## Setup

- Open a folder that is a git repository, and start a **Copilot** chat with it as the working folder.
- Create `.vscode/mcp.json` in that folder:
  ```json
  {
  	"inputs": [
  		{ "id": "log-level", "type": "promptString", "description": "Log level" },
  		{ "id": "region", "type": "promptString", "description": "Region", "default": "us-east-1" },
  		{ "id": "mode", "type": "pickString", "description": "Mode", "options": ["fast", "safe"], "default": "safe" },
  		{ "id": "token", "type": "promptString", "description": "Token", "password": true }
  	],
  	"servers": {
  		"with-inputs": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything", "--region=${input:region}"], "env": { "LOG": "${input:log-level}", "MODE": "${input:mode}" } },
  		"remote-with-input": { "type": "http", "url": "https://example.com/mcp", "headers": { "X-Region": "${input:region}" } },
  		"with-setting": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything", "--port=${config:demo.port}"] },
  		"with-oauth": { "type": "http", "url": "https://example.com/mcp", "oauth": { "clientId": "test-client" } },
  		"with-password": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything", "--token=${input:token}"] }
  	}
  }
  ```
- Add `"demo.port": 8080` to the folder's `.vscode/settings.json`.
- Commit the files, so you can see the changes with `git diff` and reset with `git checkout`.

## Scenario 1: Review the migrations

1. Open **Chat: Open Customizations** → **Migrate MCP Servers**.
2. Check that `with-inputs`, `remote-with-input`, `with-setting` and `with-oauth` can be migrated, each with a short warning:
   - inputs: *Inputs will become environment variables. Configure them in the MCP server details after migrating.*
   - settings: *Configs will become environment variables. Later changes won't apply.*
   - OAuth: *You may need to sign in again after migration.*
3. Check that `with-password` is listed as needing manual review, with a reason that password inputs can't be migrated.

## Scenario 2: Migrate

1. Select **Migrate** and confirm. The confirmation should be a warning dialog, since the servers have warnings.
2. Open `.mcp.json` at the root of the folder and check:
   - `with-inputs` uses `${REGION}`, `${LOG_LEVEL}` and `${MODE}`, and its `env` has `"LOG_LEVEL": ""`, `"REGION": "us-east-1"` and `"MODE": "safe"`. An input's default becomes the value, and an input without one is left empty for you to fill in.
   - `remote-with-input` has `"X-Region": "${REGION:-us-east-1}"`, since HTTP servers have no `env`.
   - `with-setting` uses `${DEMO_PORT}`, with `"DEMO_PORT": "8080"` in its `env`.
   - `with-oauth` has `"oauthClientId": "test-client"`.
3. Open `.vscode/mcp.json` and check that the migrated servers are gone, and that only the `token` input is left, since `with-password` still uses it. Comments and formatting elsewhere in the file are unchanged.
4. Start `with-inputs` from the MCP servers list or a Copilot chat, and check that it starts without asking for any input.

## Scenario 3: User servers

1. Run **MCP: Open User Configuration**, back up your file, and add a server that uses an input, as in the Setup.
2. Migrate it from **Migrate MCP Servers**. Besides the input warning, it should say that VS Code will ask you to trust the server again.
3. Check that it lands in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` the same way, and that you are asked to trust it again before it starts.
4. Restore your user `mcp.json` afterwards.

## Scenario 4: Settings from your user settings

1. Reset the folder with `git checkout .` and delete `.mcp.json`.
2. Move `"demo.port": 8080` from the folder's settings to your user settings.
3. Migrate `with-setting` again. Since `.mcp.json` is usually committed, a value from your user settings is not written into it: `"DEMO_PORT"` should be empty.

---

MCP servers in `.vscode/mcp.json` or your user `mcp.json` that use `${env:NAME}` can now be migrated to the Copilot configuration files. The migration rewrites each reference to `${NAME}`, so the variable is read when the server starts. **The variable's current value is never written to the file.** Migrated servers keep working in both Copilot agent sessions and VS Code's own chat.

## Setup

- Have Node.js installed. The test servers run with `npx`.
- **Quit VS Code completely.** The variables below only reach VS Code if you start it from a terminal where they're set. Running `code` while VS Code is already open reuses the old process, which doesn't have them.
- In a terminal, set the variables, create two folders, and open VS Code on the empty test folder. Use `code-insiders` instead of `code` if you're testing with Insiders.
  - macOS or Linux:
    ```sh
    export MCP_TPI_TOKEN=hello-from-env MCP_TPI_DIR="$HOME/mcp-tpi-data"
    mkdir -p "$MCP_TPI_DIR" "$HOME/mcp-tpi"
    code "$HOME/mcp-tpi"
    ```
  - Windows (PowerShell):
    ```powershell
    $env:MCP_TPI_TOKEN = 'hello-from-env'; $env:MCP_TPI_DIR = "$HOME\mcp-tpi-data"
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $env:MCP_TPI_DIR, "$HOME\mcp-tpi"
    code "$HOME\mcp-tpi"
    ```
- Trust the folder, then start a **Copilot** agent session so Copilot is the active harness. Migrations are only offered there.

## Scenario 1: Migrate workspace servers

1. Create `.vscode/mcp.json` in the test folder:
   ```json
   {
     "servers": {
       "tpi-files": {
         "command": "npx",
         "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "${env:MCP_TPI_DIR}", "${workspaceFolder}"]
       },
       "tpi-env": {
         "command": "npx",
         "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything"],
         "env": { "MCP_TPI_TOKEN": "${env:MCP_TPI_TOKEN}" }
       }
     }
   }
   ```
2. Run **Chat: Open Customizations** and open **Migrations**. Check that `tpi-files` and `tpi-env` are offered for the workspace, with `.mcp.json` as the destination.
3. Migrate them, then check:
   - both servers are gone from `.vscode/mcp.json`;
   - in `.mcp.json`, `tpi-files` has `"${MCP_TPI_DIR}"` and your test folder's full path (instead of `${workspaceFolder}`);
   - in `.mcp.json`, `tpi-env` has `"MCP_TPI_TOKEN": "${MCP_TPI_TOKEN}"`;
   - neither `hello-from-env` nor `mcp-tpi-data` appears anywhere in `.mcp.json`.

## Scenario 2: Migrated servers still work

1. In a new Copilot agent session, ask:
   - `Use the tpi-files list_allowed_directories tool.` Both your `mcp-tpi-data` folder and the test folder should be listed.
   - `Use the tpi-env get-env tool and tell me the value of MCP_TPI_TOKEN.` The answer should be `hello-from-env`.
2. Ask the same in a new **Local** agent session (VS Code's own chat). You should get the same results. This checks that VS Code itself expands `${NAME}` in `.mcp.json`.

## Scenario 3: Migrate a user server

1. Run **MCP: Open User Configuration** and add this server to `servers`:
   ```json
   "tpi-user-env": {
     "command": "npx",
     "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything"],
     "env": { "MCP_TPI_TOKEN": "${env:MCP_TPI_TOKEN}" }
   }
   ```
2. In **Migrations**, check that `tpi-user-env` is offered for your user customizations, with `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` as the destination (or `mcp-config.json` in `COPILOT_HOME` if you set it). Migrate it.
3. Check that it's gone from your user `mcp.json`, and that `mcp-config.json` has `"MCP_TPI_TOKEN": "${MCP_TPI_TOKEN}"` and doesn't contain `hello-from-env`.
4. In a new Copilot agent session and in a new Local agent session, ask `Use the tpi-user-env get-env tool and tell me the value of MCP_TPI_TOKEN.` Both should answer `hello-from-env`.

## Scenario 4: Servers that can't be migrated

1. Add these to `servers` in `.vscode/mcp.json`. They don't need to start, so errors from starting them are expected.
   ```json
   "tpi-env-name": { "command": "node", "env": { "${env:MCP_TPI_TOKEN}_KEY": "x" } },
   "tpi-bad-name": { "command": "node", "args": ["${env:my-var}"] },
   "tpi-port": { "type": "http", "url": "http://localhost:${env:MCP_TPI_PORT}/mcp" },
   "tpi-home": { "command": "node", "args": ["${userHome}"], "env": { "MCP_TPI_TOKEN": "${env:MCP_TPI_TOKEN}" } }
   ```
2. In **Migrations**, check that each server is under **Needs manual review** and nothing is migrated for it. Hover over each one to check its reason:
   - `tpi-env-name`: variables in environment variable or header names aren't supported;
   - `tpi-bad-name`: names may only contain letters, digits and underscores, and can't start with a digit;
   - `tpi-port`: environment variables aren't supported in the scheme or port of a URL;
   - `tpi-home`: the server uses a variable that can't be migrated.
3. Check that the reasons are clear and tell you how to fix the server.

## Known limitations (please don't file)

- `${env:}` in a URL host, path or query doesn't migrate yet. The server shows "The server configuration cannot be moved without changing its behavior." This is E11 in #340161.
- If a variable isn't set, VS Code passes an empty value before migration, but after migration the server receives the literal text `${NAME}` (D5 in #340161).
- The migration doesn't yet list which environment variables you need to set (E7 in #340161).

### Describe the bug

The nixpkgs `t3code` build [copies the source `package.json` and launches its directory with Electron](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/548097397d8ad3e62a4080e9ef9a0ee143e742ef/pkgs/by-name/t3/t3code/unwrapped.nix#L141-L169), preserving top-level `productName`: historically `T3 Code (Alpha)`, now `T3 Code (Beta)` [in 0.1.0](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/81493efb71e8e8244f95d3e9f71d8369654ab151/apps/desktop/package.json#L45).

Electron [prefers `productName`, then `name`](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/774d5d0a051374923758372a4ee4bf04f473151d/default_app/main.ts#L123-L129), and [captures the application name in Linux's encryption configuration](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/774d5d0a051374923758372a4ee4bf04f473151d/shell/browser/electron_browser_main_parts.cc#L649-L689).

This could lead to different safeStorage/keyring identities and decryption failure after upgrading to 0.1.0, or when switching between nixpkgs packaging and official binaries.

<!--

Please note: This issue is regarding the agent host's file watcher behavior.

-->

 

#### Description

I have been trialling the `Claude` agent harness in a repo containing the Yocto `build` tree (containing over 1M files). The `build` tree is listed in `.gitignore` and in `.vscode/settings.json` `files.watcherExclude`.

I don’t recall seeing this issue with the `Local` agent harness.

I had AI analyse the issue and this is what it said...


The `AgentHostFileMonitorService` currently ignores configured file exclusion settings. It does not honor the `files.watcherExclude` setting or respect `.gitignore` rules.

 

This causes the agent host's file watcher to monitor files, folders, and build artifacts that users have explicitly excluded. This leads to unnecessary resource consumption, high CPU usage, and potential performance degradation in large repositories or projects with high-frequency file changes (like heavy build directories or local data folders).

 

#### Proposed Solution / Request

Please update the agent host's file watcher to properly honor and inherit:

1. The `files.watcherExclude` settings defined in the user/workspace configuration.

2. The repository's `.gitignore` rules (or provide a way to opt-in/out of this behavior).

---

In case it helps, here is the LLM prompt & response:


**PROMPT**: The `files.watcherExclude` is a critical setting for controlling the number of watchers. Why is it being ignored in the `myproject` workspace?

 

**RESPONSE**:

The setting isn't being misread. The process that owns those watches never reads `files.watcherExclude` at all. I confirmed this in the VS Code Server 1.142.0 code installed on this machine (`out/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostMain.js`).

 

## Why the setting has no effect

1. **The watcher belongs to the Copilot agent host, not the workbench.** `files.watcherExclude` is applied by the normal workbench and extension-host watchers. PID 707591 was started by the agent host, which creates its own separate watcher process (`createWatcher(){ … args:["--type=fileWatcher"] … }`). It's a different client with its own requests.

2. **The agent host never reads the setting.** In that file, `files.watcherExclude` appears only inside a warning message ("Use 'files.watcherExclude' setting to exclude folders…"). Nothing reads its value, so neither your folder's `.vscode/settings.json` nor User or Machine settings can reach this watcher. That also means my earlier suggestion to copy the excludes into Machine/User settings won't help here.

3. **The recursive watch on the repo root uses a fixed exclude list.** When a session's file-changes view is open (for uncommitted or session changes), the agent host watches the session's working folder recursively:

   ```js

   _ensureRootWatcher(e,t){ … this._fileMonitorService.acquire(t, ()=>this._onRootChanged(e), {excludes:Kz, debounceMs:750}) … }

   _createEntry(…){ … this._fileService.watch(t,{recursive:!0, excludes:[...n]}) … }

   Kz = ["**/.git","**/.git/lfs/**","**/.git/logs/**","**/.git/objects/**","**/.git/subtree-cache/**",

         "**/.git/**/*.lock","**/.git/**/FETCH_HEAD","**/.git/**/fsmonitor--daemon/**","**/*.watchman-cookie-*"]

   ```

   For myproject that working folder is the git root, so everything outside `.git` gets watched. That includes the roughly 1.11M directories under `yocto/build`.

4. **`.gitignore` isn't applied either.** `git status --ignored` shows `yocto/build/` as ignored (`!!`), yet it's still watched. The exclude list is the hard-coded one above and nothing else.

 

Ten myproject agent sessions (16–18 Oct) are logged, so one of them has been holding this watch. The `remoteagent.log` you attached shows the result: since 17 Oct, other watchers have been failing with `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached`. For example, the debugpy endpoint watch and the parcel watcher on `/opt/python3.12/lib/python3.12`. That log doesn't show the cause, though; the code does.

 

I didn't find any setting that turns this watch off or adds excludes to it.

 

## What actually works, given that

- **Close or stop the myproject agent sessions** (or at least their changes view), then kill PID 707591 or restart the VS Code server. A session that's still open will set the watch up again.

- **Move the Yocto build tree out of the repo** (`TMPDIR`, `SSTATE_DIR`, `DL_DIR` and `gitrepo-cache` pointed outside `myproject` in `local.conf`). This is the only fix that doesn't depend on VS Code behaviour.

- **Run agent sessions from a smaller folder**, such as a git worktree or a subfolder without `yocto/build`. Note that the watch follows the session's working folder.

- **Report it to VS Code** (microsoft/vscode, mention "AgentHostFileMonitorService ignores files.watcherExclude") and ask for the agent host's watcher to honour `files.watcherExclude` and/or `.gitignore`.

- Raising `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` is still only a stopgap, since this watcher will grow to cover every directory it finds.

 

One thing I couldn't confirm: the minified code doesn't show exactly which UI action subscribes to the changes view. Opening the agent session and its changes/diff panel is the most likely trigger. You can test it by reopening one myproject session and watching the count with the `--terse` option of the inotify-consumers script.

Follow-up to https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/341645.

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/341700 streams a detached background shell's output into the tool call that started it, starting when that call completes. `_readDetachedShellOutput` has no other caller ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/09d2db6c2f68d373a46463bf28a8dee157cd31f3/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L8411-L8414)), so after the Agent Host or its Copilot client restarts, nothing reads a still-running detached shell's output again. Restoring that needs to reconnect each restored shell to its tool call, and the shell ID alone doesn't say which one.

**A chat can contain several shell tool calls with the same shell ID**

- After the Copilot client restarts, shell IDs can start again at `0`, so a new command can get the ID of an earlier tool call in the same chat.

**Reconnecting an older tool call settles the running shell's terminal**

- `NonPtyShellTerminalStreams._continueInBackground` treats a reused shell ID as meaning the command that held it has finished, and settles that call's terminal ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/09d2db6c2f68d373a46463bf28a8dee157cd31f3/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotNonPtyShellTerminals.ts#L636-L649)).
- A settled terminal ignores new output: `appendChunk` returns early once the stream is finalized ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/09d2db6c2f68d373a46463bf28a8dee157cd31f3/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotNonPtyShellTerminals.ts#L332)).
- So reconnecting tool calls in chat order can settle the terminal of the shell that's actually running, and its output stops appearing.

Found while prototyping restore for https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/341645.

Possible fix:

- [ ] When restoring, reconnect each running shell from `tasks.list` only to the newest tool call with its shell ID, and leave older calls with that ID settled, with a test that has two tool calls for shell `0` across a restart.

Follow-up to https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/341645.

In Agent Host Copilot chats, after the Copilot client restarts, the **Background Shells** list can show a still-running detached shell with an empty label. VS Code already had the shell's label and command, but replaces them with what the Copilot SDK's `session.rpc.tasks.list` reports, and that can be a restored shell without `description` or `command`, even though `TaskShellInfo` in `@github/copilot-sdk` types both as required strings.

- `CopilotAgentSession._toBackgroundWork` copies `label` and `command` straight from the task, with no fallback ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/09d2db6c2f68d373a46463bf28a8dee157cd31f3/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L2770-L2771)).
- After a client restart, `observeBackgroundWork` seeds the new session with the entries the chat already shows, label and command included ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/09d2db6c2f68d373a46463bf28a8dee157cd31f3/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L2696-L2707)). The next reconcile publishes the entry built from `tasks.list` over it, because the two differ ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/09d2db6c2f68d373a46463bf28a8dee157cd31f3/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L2744-L2749)).
- The **Background Shells** list renders `label` and `command` as given ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/09d2db6c2f68d373a46463bf28a8dee157cd31f3/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostBackgroundShells.ts#L29-L30)).

Seen in a local prototype for https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/341645. The code above is unchanged on `main`.

Possible fix:

- [ ] In `_toBackgroundWork`, fall back to the `label` and `command` of the entry already in `_backgroundWork` when the task has none, with a test that restores a detached shell whose task has neither.
